name: @argszero/dsh-destructive-command-guard
description: Refuses a shell command before it runs when it deletes something it did not name. In PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive and the automatic variables are read-only, so `$home = "<scratch>"` followed by `Remove-Item $home -Recurse -Force` removes the operator's real profile: the assignment fails silently, `$ErrorActionPreference` defaults to `Continue`, and the command contains no dangerous path for a pattern to find. This plugin decides on the two facts that are certain from the text — an automatic-variable name assigned and then used as a deletion operand, and a recursive or forced deletion whose operand is a home reference ($HOME, $home, ~, $env:USERPROFILE) or a filesystem root — and refuses the call at tools/pre-execute, before the body runs and before any approval prompt. It refuses nothing else: deleting a variable, however ordinary, is not what makes a command dangerous. Zero runtime dependencies, no sandbox changes, fail-open when its own scan errors.
